subproblem.title: Fixed-scale comparison of the blow-up integrals of A ⊆ B (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 "⇒")
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let A ⊆ B ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel sets, x ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0 and R, C ∈ ℝ. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous with |f(y)| ≤ C for every y and f(y) = 0 for every y ∉ closedBall(0, R). Write η = blowUpMap x r, so η(z) = r⁻¹·(z − x) (SimonGMT Chapter03), and μ = μHE[n]. If μ(η(B) ∩ closedBall(0, R)) < ∞, then |∫_{η(B)} f dμ − ∫_{η(A)} f dμ| ≤ C · μ(η(B ∖ A) ∩ closedBall(0, R)). The measure on the right is finite and is converted to a real number by ENNReal.toReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (A B : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (r R C : ℝ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ), Continuous f → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → 0 < r → μHE[n] (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' B ∩ closedBall 0 R) ≠ ∞ → (∀ y : Euclid P, ‖f y‖ ≤ C) → (∀ y : Euclid P, y ∉ closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R → f y = 0) → ‖(∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' B, f y ∂μHE[n]) - ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' A, f y ∂μHE[n]‖ ≤ C * (μHE[n] (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' (B \ A) ∩ closedBall 0 R)).toReal
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (book/chapter-03.txt lines 113-141). There the integral of f over η_{x,λ}(M) is split into integrals over the blow-ups of disjoint pieces, and the integral over the blow-up of a piece is bounded by sup|f| · H^n(B_R(0) ∩ η_{x,λ}(piece)) when f vanishes off B_R(0). This child is Steps 1, 3, 4 and the first half of Step 5 of the parent proof, at one fixed scale r.

Notation: μ := μHE[n]; η := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, so η(z) = r⁻¹·(z − x); K := closedBall(0, R). For a set S, ∫_S f dμ is the Bochner integral of f with respect to μ restricted to S. Since r > 0, r ≠ 0.

1. (η is injective.) Suppose η(z) = η(w), i.e. r⁻¹·(z − x) = r⁻¹·(w − x). Multiply by r and use r·r⁻¹ = 1 to get z − x = w − x, hence z = w.

2. (Images under η are preimages under a continuous affine map, hence Borel.) Let g(y) := x + r·y. We claim η(T) = g⁻¹(T) for every T ⊆ ℝ^P.
- If y = η(z) with z ∈ T, then g(y) = x + r·(r⁻¹·(z − x)) = x + (z − x) = z ∈ T.
- Conversely, if g(y) ∈ T, then η(g(y)) = r⁻¹·((x + r·y) − x) = r⁻¹·(r·y) = y, so y ∈ η(T).
The map g is continuous, hence Borel measurable, so η(T) = g⁻¹(T) is Borel whenever T is Borel. In particular η(A), η(B) and η(B ∖ A) are Borel; B ∖ A is Borel as a difference of Borel sets.

3. (Integrability on η(T) for Borel T ⊆ B.) Let T be Borel with T ⊆ B.
- η(T) ∩ K ⊆ η(B) ∩ K, so μ(η(T) ∩ K) ≤ μ(η(B) ∩ K) < ∞ by hypothesis.
- f is continuous, hence (a.e.-strongly) measurable, and |f(y)| ≤ C for every y. A measurable function bounded by a constant is integrable on a set of finite measure (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded`). So f is integrable on η(T) ∩ K.
- Every y ∈ η(T) ∖ (η(T) ∩ K) lies outside K, so f(y) = 0 by hypothesis. Since η(T) is measurable (Step 2), integrability extends from η(T) ∩ K to η(T) (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.IntegrableOn.of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero`).
We use this with T = A (as A ⊆ B) and with T = B ∖ A.

4. (Splitting.) Because A ⊆ B, B = A ∪ (B ∖ A), hence η(B) = η(A) ∪ η(B ∖ A); the image of a union is the union of the images.
- A and B ∖ A are disjoint and η is injective (Step 1), so η(A) and η(B ∖ A) are disjoint.
- η(B ∖ A) is measurable (Step 2).
- f is integrable on η(A) and on η(B ∖ A) (Step 3).
By additivity of the set integral over a disjoint union (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.setIntegral_union`),
   ∫_{η(B)} f dμ = ∫_{η(A)} f dμ + ∫_{η(B∖A)} f dμ,
so ∫_{η(B)} f dμ − ∫_{η(A)} f dμ = ∫_{η(B∖A)} f dμ.

5. (Localization to K.) Put S := η(B ∖ A) ∩ K. Then S ⊆ η(B ∖ A), η(B ∖ A) is measurable, and f vanishes on η(B ∖ A) ∖ S because those points lie outside K. Hence ∫_{η(B∖A)} f dμ = ∫_S f dμ (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero`).

6. (Estimate.) Since B ∖ A ⊆ B, S ⊆ η(B) ∩ K, so μ(S) ≤ μ(η(B) ∩ K) < ∞. Also |f(y)| ≤ C for all y ∈ S. Therefore |∫_S f dμ| ≤ C · μ.real(S), where μ.real(S) = (μ(S)).toReal (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const`, which requires μ(S) < ∞). No sign condition on C or R is used. The cited lemma needs only μ(S) < ∞ and the pointwise bound on S. If R < 0, then K = S = ∅ and both sides are 0.

7. (Conclusion.) Combining Steps 4-6,
   |∫_{η(B)} f dμ − ∫_{η(A)} f dμ| = |∫_{η(B∖A)} f dμ| = |∫_S f dμ| ≤ C · (μ(η(B ∖ A) ∩ closedBall(0, R))).toReal.
This is the asserted inequality; for f : ℝ^P → ℝ the norm ‖·‖ is the absolute value. ∎
proof_key_steps: η = blowUpMap x r is injective (r ≠ 0) and η(T) = (y ↦ x + r·y)⁻¹(T), so η maps Borel sets to Borel sets.
For Borel T ⊆ B, f is integrable on η(T). It is bounded by C on η(T) ∩ closedBall(0,R), a set of measure ≤ μHE[n](η(B) ∩ closedBall(0,R)) < ∞, and it vanishes on the rest of the measurable set η(T).
η(B) is the disjoint union of η(A) and η(B∖A), so setIntegral_union gives ∫_{η(B)} f − ∫_{η(A)} f = ∫_{η(B∖A)} f.
Since f = 0 off closedBall(0,R), ∫_{η(B∖A)} f = ∫_{η(B∖A) ∩ closedBall(0,R)} f. norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const bounds this by C·(μHE[n](η(B∖A) ∩ closedBall(0,R))).toReal.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the prose and hypotheses. The proof establishes injectivity and Borel images, then finite localized mass and integrability before applying disjoint-union additivity. Vanishing outside the ball justifies localization, and the finite-measure integral bound gives precisely the stated toReal inequality. Arbitrary R and C require no additional hypotheses. Every step is supplied without circular reliance.

subproblem.title: Rescaling a vanishing n-density quotient: (ofReal r)⁻ⁿ · g(r·R) → 0
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, g : ℝ → [0, ∞] and R > 0. If g(ρ)/ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^n → 0 in [0, ∞] as ρ → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>]0), then (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹^n · g(r·R) → 0 in [0, ∞] as r → 0⁺.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (R : ℝ), 0 < R → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => g ρ / ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ ^ n * g (r * R)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the final limit in Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (book/chapter-03.txt lines 127-141): sup|f| · λ^{-n} H^n(B_{λR}(x) ∩ ·) → 0 when the set has zero n-density at x. This child is the [0, ∞]-valued part of Steps 5-6 of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary function g; the parent uses g(ρ) = μHE[n]((B ∖ A) ∩ closedBall(x, ρ)). All arithmetic below is in [0, ∞] = ℝ≥0∞, and r → 0⁺ means convergence along the filter 𝓝[>]0.

1. (The substitution ρ = r·R maps 𝓝[>]0 to 𝓝[>]0.) Let h(r) := r·R.
- h is continuous and h(0) = 0·R = 0, so h(r) → 0 as r → 0. Since 𝓝[>]0 ≤ 𝓝 0, also h(r) → 0 along 𝓝[>]0.
- Eventually along 𝓝[>]0 we have r > 0, because (0, ∞) belongs to 𝓝[>]0. Then h(r) = r·R > 0, because R > 0.
A function that tends to 0 and eventually takes values in (0, ∞) tends to 0 within (0, ∞) (Mathlib `tendsto_nhdsWithin_of_tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_within`). Hence h tends from 𝓝[>]0 to 𝓝[>]0.

2. (Composition.) Composing the hypothesis with h (Step 1) gives g(r·R)/ENNReal.ofReal(r·R)^n → 0 as r → 0⁺.

3. (Multiplication by a finite constant.) Put c := ENNReal.ofReal(R)^n. It is finite, because ENNReal.ofReal(R) < ∞. Multiplication by a finite constant preserves convergence in [0, ∞] (Mathlib `ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul`, applicable since c ≠ ∞). So c · [g(r·R)/ENNReal.ofReal(r·R)^n] → c · 0 = 0 as r → 0⁺.

4. (Algebraic identity for r > 0.) Fix r > 0 and set a := ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n and b := ENNReal.ofReal(R)^n = c.
- Because r > 0 and R > 0, ENNReal.ofReal(r) and ENNReal.ofReal(R) are positive and finite, so a and b are nonzero and finite.
- Because r ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal(r·R) = ENNReal.ofReal(r)·ENNReal.ofReal(R) (Mathlib `ENNReal.ofReal_mul`). Hence ENNReal.ofReal(r·R)^n = a·b.
Write division as multiplication by the inverse (u/v = v⁻¹·u). The rule (a·b)⁻¹ = a⁻¹·b⁻¹ holds because a ≠ 0 and a ≠ ∞ (Mathlib `ENNReal.mul_inv`). With commutativity and associativity, and b·b⁻¹ = 1 because b ≠ 0 and b ≠ ∞ (Mathlib `ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel`), we get
   b · (g(r·R)/(a·b)) = b · (a⁻¹ · b⁻¹ · g(r·R)) = (b · b⁻¹) · a⁻¹ · g(r·R) = a⁻¹ · g(r·R).
Finally a⁻¹ = (ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n)⁻¹ = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹^n (Mathlib `ENNReal.inv_pow`). Thus for every r > 0,
   c · [g(r·R)/ENNReal.ofReal(r·R)^n] = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹^n · g(r·R).
All manipulations are identities in [0, ∞], so they also hold when g(r·R) = ∞.

5. (Conclusion.) By Step 4, the function of Step 3 agrees with r ↦ (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹^n · g(r·R) on (0, ∞), a set belonging to 𝓝[>]0, so the two are eventually equal along 𝓝[>]0. Eventually equal functions have the same limits (Mathlib `Filter.Tendsto.congr'`). Hence (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹^n · g(r·R) → 0 as r → 0⁺. ∎
proof_key_steps: r ↦ r·R is continuous, vanishes at 0 and is positive for r > 0 (R > 0), so it maps 𝓝[>]0 into 𝓝[>]0.
Composing the hypothesis gives g(rR)/ofReal(rR)^n → 0. Multiplying by the finite constant ofReal(R)^n keeps the limit 0.
For r > 0, ofReal(rR)^n = ofReal(r)^n·ofReal(R)^n with both factors in (0,∞), so ofReal(R)^n·(g(rR)/ofReal(rR)^n) = (ofReal r)⁻¹^n·g(rR).
The two functions agree eventually along 𝓝[>]0, so the limit 0 transfers by Tendsto.congr'.

audit.reason: The prose and one-line ENNReal proposition agree. Positive R makes r ↦ rR preserve the right-neighborhood filter. Composition and multiplication by the finite constant ofReal(R)^n give the limit; cancellation uses explicitly nonzero finite factors and transfers by eventual equality. The argument remains valid for n = 0 and infinite values of g. No undeclared dependency or missing proof step occurs.

subproblem.title: Asymptotically equal blow-up integrals give equal approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let M, M' ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets and x ∈ ℝ^P. Write η_r = blowUpMap x r and μ = μHE[n]. Suppose that for every compactly supported continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{η_r(M)} f dμ − ∫_{η_r(M')} f dμ → 0 as r → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>]0). Then for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4) if and only if M' does.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M M' : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P), (∀ f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Euclid P) ℝ, Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => (∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M, f y ∂μHE[n]) - ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M', f y ∂μHE[n]) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)) → ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (book/chapter-03.txt lines 77-84) and the last step of the proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (lines 117-143). There, once the blow-up integrals over two sets differ by terms tending to 0, "T_x M exists and = T_x N_j". This child is Step 7 of the parent proof, stated for two arbitrary sets.

Notation: μ := μHE[n] and η_r := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r. For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), i.e. f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Euclid P) ℝ, and r ∈ ℝ, put I(r) := ∫_{η_r(M)} f dμ, I'(r) := ∫_{η_r(M')} f dμ, D(r) := I(r) − I'(r), and L := ∫_Q f dμ, the integral over the set Q. By hypothesis D(r) → 0 along 𝓝[>]0 for every such f.

1. (Definition.) By the definition in SimonGMT Chapter03, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q holds iff finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), I(r) → L along 𝓝[>]0. The same holds for M' with I'(r) in place of I(r). The condition finrank Q = n does not involve M or M', so it is the same on both sides.

2. (⇒) Assume HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. Then finrank Q = n. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). We have I(r) → L and D(r) → 0 along 𝓝[>]0. By the limit of a difference of real-valued functions, I(r) − D(r) → L − 0 = L. For every r, I(r) − D(r) = I(r) − (I(r) − I'(r)) = I'(r). Hence I'(r) → L along 𝓝[>]0. Since f was arbitrary, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q holds.

3. (⇐) Assume HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q. Then finrank Q = n. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). We have I'(r) → L and D(r) → 0, so I'(r) + D(r) → L + 0 = L. For every r, I'(r) + D(r) = I'(r) + (I(r) − I'(r)) = I(r). Hence I(r) → L along 𝓝[>]0, and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q holds.

4. Steps 2 and 3 give the equivalence, for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unfold Simon Definition 1.4 (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt): finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c, ∫_{η_r(·)} f dμHE[n] → ∫_Q f dμHE[n] along 𝓝[>]0. The dimension condition is common to both sides.

audit.reason: The exact type matches the prose for arbitrary sets and all compactly supported continuous real test functions. Unfolding the pinned definition gives the stated common dimension condition and integral limits. Subtracting the vanishing difference proves the forward implication; adding it proves the reverse. No measurability or integrability assumption is needed for this definitional transfer, and the proof is complete and non-circular.
